races.name: South West Rail Solutions Ltd. "National Hunt" Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Limier d'Arthel

runners_data.name: Handmedownastar

runners_data.name: Dutch Corner

runners_data.name: Docteur Romeo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who pulled up last time and has faded in recent finishes, question marks over stamina despite decent official rating

runners_data.name: JPR Two
runners_data.note: Another who fades in the finish returning from 120-day break, Paul Nicholls booking Freddie Gingell suggests some confidence remains

runners_data.name: Dante's Rocco
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was close third last time, 5lb claimer Paddy Hanlon provides valuable weight relief for Syd Hosie's 3/16 strike rate

runners_data.name: Saffron Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who has faded badly in recent starts, 7lb claimer helps but Sue Gardner's 0/5 record and poor recent form are concerning

runners_data.name: Warfleet
runners_data.note: Natural leader returning from 394-day absence with headgear, Jimmy Frost's booking of Conor O'Farrell suggests belief in comeback ability

runners_data.name: Poet's Muse
runners_data.note: Front-runner from lower grade with modest ratings, Lorcan Williams continues association and recent fourth suggests some improvement

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 109-day break with solid past form, Finn Lambert's 3lb claim valuable but David Brace's 0/1 record noted

runners_data.name: Mrs Pen
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who fades badly in finishes, 7lb claimer Chad Bament provides maximum relief but form figures are deeply concerning

races.paceDynamic: Warfleet and Poet's Muse will dispute the early lead, with Warfleet returning from a 394-day absence potentially keen to use his natural speed. The pace should be genuine with Limier d'Arthel, Handmedownastar, Dutch Corner, Docteur Romeo and JPR Two all comfortable racing prominently behind the leaders. This will stretch the field and create a strong gallop over the testing 2m2½f trip on soft ground. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses — the pace is genuine and the willing pace-setters will ensure the field is strung out for closers to pick off tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine with Warfleet and Poet's Muse going too fast early
scenarios.body: The soft ground and strong gallop will find out the pace-setters, allowing the hold-up horses to sweep past in the final furlong. Harry Fry's excellent 3/9 record and Dan Skelton's 9/40 strike rate suggest their runners are primed for big efforts.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders set only a steady pace and the prominent horses get first run
scenarios.body: Limier d'Arthel and Handmedownastar can capitalize on their forward positions to steal a march on the hold-up brigade. The good-to-soft conditions suit both horses perfectly based on their recent form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Mid-Division
scenarios.trigger: If Warfleet's long absence tells and Poet's Muse folds early leaving no pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the back of the last hurdle with mid-division runners getting the perfect setup. Dutch Corner's consistency and Dante's Rocco's recent proximity to winners would make them dangerous.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Warfleet handles his return better than expected and gets an easy lead
scenarios.body: Jimmy Frost's runner could dictate terms and prove hard to peg back if the field allows him too much rope early. His headgear suggests connections expect improvement from his long break.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Warfleet gets an uncontested lead early - his 394-day absence could work in his favor if allowed to dictate terms
Monitor Hardly Surprising's market moves given Harry Fry's excellent 3/9 strike rate and the horse's strong RPR of 124
Keep an eye on Dutch Corner's jumping under pressure as Dan Skelton's 9/40 record suggests this hold-up horse is primed
Watch for any non-runners as several horses including Docteur Romeo, JPR Two and Saffron Belle have recent fading form
Observe how the inexperienced claiming jockeys handle the pace early, particularly Pritchard on Limier d'Arthel switching from experienced pilot

races.name: Les Drew Hello Matey I'm 80 Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Ideallko

runners_data.name: Begin The Luck

runners_data.name: Jack's A Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from 311-day absence but won last time on heavy ground, Miss Mathias' 7lb claim significant but Tim Vaughan struggling for winners

runners_data.name: Jack Doyen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying just 148lbs with recent winning form, Jack Quinlan booking suggests stable confidence despite low official rating

runners_data.name: Firefly Lane
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finished third over course and distance last time, low weight of 142lbs could be decisive but poor recent TopSpeed figure concerning

runners_data.name: Palawan Du Mazet
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two recent wins including one on soft ground, handles the going well but Alan Jones has no runners in last 14 days

runners_data.name: Devilsrollthedice
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making handicap debut for Gordon Treacy, no RPR or TopSpeed data makes assessment difficult but headgear applied previously

runners_data.name: Tractor Jack
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from powerful Joe Tizzard yard but has clear stamina doubts having faded in recent finishes over similar distances

races.paceDynamic: Begin The Luck will lead from the start with Firefly Lane, Devilsrollthedice and Tractor Jack providing early company in the prominent positions. The pace will be sustainable rather than cut-throat with only one confirmed front-runner, allowing Begin The Luck to dictate terms without immediate pressure. The majority hold-up horses (Ideallko, Jack's A Legend, Jack Doyen, Palawan Du Mazet) will be content to track the leaders through the early stages. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses — the genuine but manageable pace will string the field out and create opportunities for closers to pick off tired leaders in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Begin The Luck sets sustainable fractions without serious pressure from the prominent group
scenarios.body: The pace becomes perfect for the closers who can time their runs perfectly as the leaders tire from the second-last fence. Ideallko and Jack Doyen, both fresh and capable, benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group applies more pressure than expected, creating a faster tempo throughout
scenarios.body: Begin The Luck gets company from Firefly Lane or Devilsrollthedice, quickening the pace and potentially catching the hold-up horses flat-footed. The prominently-ridden horses can then kick clear before the closers get organised.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the sustainable pace becomes crawling slow with no one willing to commit early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last fence where class and finishing speed matter most, potentially suiting the highest-rated horses regardless of style. Jack Doyen's low weight becomes crucial in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Begin The Luck makes an error or gets headed early, leaving no clear leader
scenarios.body: The race fragments with multiple pace changes that can catch horses out of position, creating opportunities for those who adapt best. Tractor Jack's tendency to fade late becomes less relevant in a messy tactical affair.

watchPoints.text: Tractor Jack has faded badly in his last two runs over similar distances and could stop quickly if the pace becomes testing
Jack's A Legend returns from a 311-day break which could leave him short of peak fitness despite his trainer's positive signals
Begin The Luck must handle the responsibility of leadership as he's shown some inconsistency when pressed by other front-runners
Watch for early market moves on Devilsrollthedice who lacks public form figures but could be well-handicapped on debut for new connections
Firefly Lane's recent TopSpeed figure of just 30 suggests a significant drop in ability that makes the third-place finish last time misleading

races.name: South West Rail Solutions Ltd. Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Northern Air
runners_data.note: Recent Newton Abbot winner returning from 94-day break with Tom Broughton's 5lb claim helping offset the 168lbs burden

runners_data.name: Green Sky
runners_data.note: David Pipe-trained front runner carrying first-time cheekpieces after disappointing recent efforts, could benefit from uncontested lead

runners_data.name: Jackeline

runners_data.name: Parikarma

runners_data.name: Reel Orange
runners_data.note: Joe Tizzard's 3/24 strike rate provides confidence, well-handicapped on 155lbs with first-time tongue tie applied

runners_data.name: Getarose
runners_data.note: Unexposed five-year-old on attractive 148lbs minimum weight, though limited experience on soft going could be crucial

runners_data.name: Eskimo Sam
runners_data.note: Warning signs of fading in recent finishes make him vulnerable despite the 153lbs mark, needs to prove stamina holds

races.paceDynamic: Green Sky is the only confirmed front runner in this small field and should get an uncontested lead, setting a comfortable rhythm over this 2m1f trip. With all seven runners classified as hold-up horses, there's minimal early pace pressure, allowing Green Sky to dictate terms throughout. The lack of prominent racers means the pace will likely be steady rather than searching, with the field bunching up approaching the home turn. This setup moderately favours hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick — the sustainable pace will keep the field together, creating a sprint finish where class and current form will prove decisive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Green Sky sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The field stays bunched and it becomes a sprint finish where the classiest hold-up horses with current form prevail. Northern Air and Jackeline, both showing recent winning form, can unleash their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Green Sky's uncontested lead proves decisive and the hold-up horses fail to reel him in
scenarios.body: Despite his hold-up style, Green Sky uses the lack of pace pressure to his advantage and stays on strongly up the hill. His RPR of 106 and David Pipe's expertise with front runners could see him reverse recent disappointing form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Improvers
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace allows progressive types to close strongly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Getarose and Reel Orange, both carrying light weights and trained by in-form yards, time their challenges perfectly. Joe Tizzard's 3/24 recent record and the 13lb weight advantage for Getarose could prove telling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fading Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of genuine early pace results in a crawling gallop that nobody can quicken from
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical affair where positioning matters more than finishing speed, and horses with recent course experience or tactical pace hold sway. Northern Air's Newton Abbot win and Parikarma's consistency could benefit.

watchPoints.text: Green Sky's front-running tactics could backfire if the first-time cheekpieces make him too keen early
Northern Air's 94-day absence since his course win may leave him needing the run despite his obvious class advantage
Getarose's light weight and progressive profile could be significant if she handles the step up in class
Reel Orange's recent pull-up raises fitness concerns despite returning quickly from his last run just 10 days ago
The good to soft going conditions suit most of these but could expose Getarose's limited soft ground experience

races.name: Happy 45th Birthday Andy Hurtley Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tahmuras

runners_data.name: Scarface
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but recent third-place finish suggests he may be just below this level despite Joe Tizzard's solid 14-day record

runners_data.name: Royal Jewel
runners_data.note: In-form prominent racer with a recent win and Philip Hobbs stable firing, well-positioned tactically for this pace scenario

runners_data.name: Calimystic

runners_data.name: Kap Ouest
runners_data.note: Only genuine hold-up horse with headgear retained and Harry Fry's strong recent strike rate suggesting stable confidence in this approach

runners_data.name: Nickelforce
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 147-day break for struggling trainer Ben Case, will need significant improvement from this layoff

runners_data.name: Hardy Du Seuil

runners_data.name: Bumpy Evans
runners_data.note: Natural front runner returning after 167 days for Kerry Lee with no recent winners, will need to maintain gallop under pressure

races.paceDynamic: Bumpy Evans will lead from the front with no other natural pace-setters in this field, creating a moderate tempo that won't stretch this small field early. The six prominent racers (Tahmuras, Scarface, Royal Jewel, Calimystic, Nickelforce, Hardy Du Seuil) will track in a compact group behind the leader, while only Kap Ouest sits as a genuine hold-up horse. With sustainable fractions and a short run-in at Newton Abbot, horses that can position prominently and maintain their pitch will have the tactical edge. This setup moderately favours prominent racers who can stay close to the pace without being pressured early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Bumpy Evans sets a steady tempo and the prominent pack stays bunched
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between the well-positioned prominent runners, with form horses having every chance to show their class. Tahmuras and Calimystic can utilise their quality, while Royal Jewel's recent winning form gives him strong claims.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bumpy Evans slows significantly in the straight and creates a messy finish
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows all horses to stay in contention, turning it into a scramble where any horse can win on the day. This chaotic finish could see an outsider like Nickelforce or Hardy Du Seuil strike gold.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Bumpy Evans gets an easy lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage before the field can respond, with his recent good form at this distance proving decisive. The prominent racers' inability to pressure early costs them dearly in a tactical error.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens unexpectedly and the prominent pack goes too hard
scenarios.body: Kap Ouest benefits from being the only genuine closer as the early pace tells on the leaders in the straight. His trainer Harry Fry's good recent form (3/9 in 14 days) suggests he's found the key to this horse.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Bumpy Evans gets an uncontested lead early - could steal a march on this field if allowed to dictate fractions
Monitor Tahmuras for ring rustiness after 78 days off despite Paul Nicholls' skill with returning horses
Observe Calimystic's jumping rhythm early as his recent wins suggest he's peaking at the right time
Check if Kap Ouest gets the strong pace he needs as the only closer in a field full of prominent racers
Watch Nickelforce for signs of a pipe-opener given his 147-day absence and trainer's poor recent form

runners_data.name: Striking A Pose
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying bottom weight of 155lbs, but disappointing recent form with no wins on similar going from 15 attempts is concerning

runners_data.name: Rickety Bridge
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but 42 days since last run under Paul Nicholls who's firing at 12% with his runners, headgear retained suggests issues

runners_data.name: Crossgales King
runners_data.note: Most recent winner on Soft ground just 30 days ago, Syd Hosie's 19% strike rate and claimer Callum Pritchard's 3lb allowance helps his chances

runners_data.name: Top Guy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with excellent Soft ground record, Dan Skelton's 21% strike rate and strong recent form make him a leading contender

runners_data.name: Sam's Amour
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 99 days off for Keiran Burke who's 0/5 recently, long absence is a major concern

runners_data.name: Walk Tall
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying just 152lbs, but form figures show decline and Joe Tizzard's moderate 13% strike rate offers little confidence

races.paceDynamic: Call Me Legend looks the clear pace-setter with his prominent style and recent front-running form, likely to dictate from the front without serious pressure early on. The majority of this field (Striking A Pose, Rickety Bridge, Crossgales King, Sam's Amour) are prominent racers who will settle just behind, creating a solid gallop but not frantic early pace. Top Guy and Walk Tall as the designated hold-up horses will be tracking from the rear, while Kruger Park is a non-runner. This setup moderately favours the hold-up horses — the pace will be genuine enough to stretch the field over this extended trip, but not so strong as to compromise stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses strike late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays honest throughout and the prominent horses come under pressure from 2f out
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop will string out the field and allow the patient riders to pick off tiring leaders in the final half-mile. Top Guy's excellent soft ground record (1W4P from 10 runs) and Walk Tall's light weight become crucial advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner dominates throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend establishes an uncontested lead and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: His recent winning form and Philip Hobbs' 3/14 strike rate suggest he's primed for another front-running display. The prominent horses behind fail to mount a serious challenge on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent horse times run perfectly
scenarios.trigger: If one of the mid-pack prominent runners gets the perfect trip and strikes approaching the last
scenarios.body: Crossgales King's recent Soft ground win and light racing schedule make him the most likely beneficiary. His 164lbs handicap mark looks workable after that impressive last-start victory.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend goes too slow early and the race becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The prominent horses get first run but lack the turn of foot needed in a slowly-run contest. This would be unusual over 3m2½f on testing ground.

watchPoints.text: Call Me Legend if he gets an easy lead early - his front-running style could prove unstoppable with Philip Hobbs' horses running well
Top Guy's jumping under pressure in the home straight - his hold-up style means he needs to be fluent at the business end
Crossgales King's stamina over this extended 3m2½f trip having won last time over 2m4f - the step up is significant
The pace through the middle section - if it's too steady it will compromise the hold-up horses' chances significantly
Ground conditions if they deteriorate further during racing - several runners have question marks over Heavy going
